_meta.description: MedGuard curated drug-drug interaction seed dataset.
_meta.note: Each entry uses lowercase active ingredient names (post-normalization). Keys are sorted alphabetically for consistent lookup.

interactions.title: Major Bleeding Risk: Warfarin + Ibuprofen
interactions.detail: Ibuprofen (an NSAID) inhibits platelet aggregation and damages the stomach lining. Combined with warfarin (a blood thinner), this dramatically increases the risk of serious gastrointestinal bleeding and stroke.

interactions.title: Major Bleeding Risk: Warfarin + Aspirin
interactions.detail: Aspirin inhibits platelets and can cause stomach ulcers. When combined with warfarin, the risk of internal bleeding — especially in the stomach and brain — increases significantly. This combination should only be used under strict medical supervision.

interactions.title: Major Bleeding Risk: Warfarin + Naproxen
interactions.detail: Naproxen is an NSAID similar to ibuprofen. It inhibits platelet function and irritates the stomach lining, greatly amplifying the anticoagulant effect of warfarin and raising the risk of life-threatening bleeding.

interactions.title: Dangerous Potassium Buildup: Lisinopril + Potassium Supplements
interactions.detail: Lisinopril is an ACE inhibitor that causes the kidneys to retain potassium. Taking additional potassium supplements can push blood potassium levels dangerously high (hyperkalemia), which can cause life-threatening heart rhythm problems and cardiac arrest.

interactions.title: Severe Hyperkalemia Risk: Lisinopril + Spironolactone
interactions.detail: Both lisinopril (ACE inhibitor) and spironolactone (potassium-sparing diuretic) reduce potassium excretion through different mechanisms. Together, they cause dangerous potassium accumulation in the blood, risking fatal cardiac arrhythmia.

interactions.title: Kidney Failure Risk: Metformin + Iodinated Contrast
interactions.detail: Iodinated contrast dye (used in CT scans and angiography) can temporarily impair kidney function. In patients taking metformin, this can cause lactic acidosis — a dangerous buildup of lactic acid in the blood that can be fatal.
interactions.source: FDA Label / Radiological Society of North America

interactions.title: Severe Muscle Damage: Simvastatin + Clarithromycin
interactions.detail: Clarithromycin (an antibiotic) blocks the liver enzyme (CYP3A4) that breaks down simvastatin. This causes simvastatin levels in the blood to spike dramatically, leading to rhabdomyolysis — a severe breakdown of muscle tissue that can cause kidney failure.

interactions.title: Severe Muscle Damage Risk: Simvastatin + Erythromycin
interactions.detail: Like clarithromycin, erythromycin inhibits the CYP3A4 enzyme that metabolizes simvastatin. This leads to dangerous accumulation of simvastatin and serious risk of muscle breakdown (rhabdomyolysis).

interactions.title: Increased Bleeding Risk: Sertraline (SSRI) + Ibuprofen
interactions.detail: SSRIs like sertraline reduce platelet serotonin stores, impairing clotting. When combined with NSAIDs like ibuprofen, the risk of gastrointestinal bleeding increases by 3–15 times compared to taking either drug alone.

interactions.title: Increased Bleeding Risk: Fluoxetine (SSRI) + Ibuprofen
interactions.detail: Fluoxetine is an SSRI antidepressant. Like all SSRIs, it depletes platelet serotonin and reduces clotting ability. Combined with ibuprofen's anti-platelet effect, this significantly raises gastrointestinal bleeding risk.

interactions.title: Life-Threatening Serotonin Syndrome: Sertraline + Tramadol
interactions.detail: Tramadol increases serotonin levels in the brain. Combined with sertraline (an SSRI), this can trigger serotonin syndrome — a dangerous condition causing agitation, rapid heart rate, high blood pressure, and in severe cases, seizures and death.

interactions.title: Life-Threatening Serotonin Syndrome: Fluoxetine + Tramadol
interactions.detail: Fluoxetine strongly inhibits the metabolism of tramadol AND increases serotonin. This double effect makes the combination extremely dangerous, with a very high risk of serotonin syndrome.

interactions.title: Dangerous Heart Block: Metoprolol + Verapamil
interactions.detail: Metoprolol (a beta-blocker) and verapamil (a calcium channel blocker) both slow the heart rate and reduce heart muscle contraction through different mechanisms. Together, they can cause dangerously slow heart rates, heart block, and potentially cardiac arrest.

interactions.title: Elevated Statin Levels: Atorvastatin + Clarithromycin
interactions.detail: Clarithromycin inhibits the CYP3A4 enzyme that processes atorvastatin in the liver. This raises atorvastatin blood levels and increases the risk of myopathy (muscle pain and weakness) and rhabdomyolysis.

interactions.title: Digoxin Toxicity: Digoxin + Amiodarone
interactions.detail: Amiodarone significantly raises digoxin blood levels by competing for the same elimination pathway. Digoxin has a very narrow therapeutic window — even a small increase can cause toxicity: nausea, vision changes, and life-threatening arrhythmias.

interactions.title: Reduced Blood Thinner Effect: Clopidogrel + Omeprazole
interactions.detail: Omeprazole (a proton pump inhibitor) blocks CYP2C19, the liver enzyme that activates clopidogrel (a blood thinner used to prevent clots). This can reduce clopidogrel's effectiveness by up to 40%, increasing the risk of heart attack or stroke in at-risk patients.

interactions.title: Dangerous Anticoagulation: Warfarin + Fluconazole
interactions.detail: Fluconazole (an antifungal) powerfully inhibits the CYP2C9 enzyme that breaks down warfarin. This causes warfarin blood levels to rise sharply, dramatically increasing the risk of severe, potentially fatal bleeding.

interactions.title: Increased Bleeding Risk: Ciprofloxacin + Warfarin
interactions.detail: Ciprofloxacin (a fluoroquinolone antibiotic) inhibits warfarin metabolism and can disrupt gut bacteria that produce Vitamin K, both of which amplify warfarin's anticoagulant effect. INR can rise dangerously within days of starting ciprofloxacin.

interactions.title: Elevated Statin Levels: Amlodipine + Simvastatin
interactions.detail: Amlodipine (a calcium channel blocker) weakly inhibits the CYP3A4 pathway that metabolizes simvastatin. This can raise simvastatin blood concentrations and modestly increase the risk of myopathy. FDA recommends limiting simvastatin to 20mg/day with amlodipine.

interactions.title: Lithium Toxicity: Lithium + Ibuprofen
interactions.detail: NSAIDs like ibuprofen reduce kidney blood flow, causing the kidneys to retain lithium instead of excreting it. Lithium has an extremely narrow therapeutic window — even a modest rise in blood levels can cause tremors, confusion, seizures, and kidney damage.

interactions.title: Lithium Toxicity: Lithium + Naproxen
interactions.detail: Like ibuprofen, naproxen (an NSAID) impairs kidney lithium excretion, causing dangerous lithium accumulation. This combination requires immediate medical review.

interactions.title: Methotrexate Toxicity: Methotrexate + Ibuprofen
interactions.detail: NSAIDs like ibuprofen compete with methotrexate for kidney excretion, causing methotrexate to accumulate to toxic levels. This can cause severe bone marrow suppression, liver damage, and dangerous mouth sores.

interactions.title: Complex Interaction: Phenytoin + Warfarin
interactions.detail: Phenytoin (anti-epileptic) and warfarin interact in both directions: phenytoin initially raises warfarin levels (bleeding risk), then over weeks it induces liver enzymes that lower warfarin levels (clot risk). This unpredictable interaction requires very close INR monitoring.

interactions.title: Increased Anticoagulation: Allopurinol + Warfarin
interactions.detail: Allopurinol (used for gout) inhibits the breakdown of warfarin, causing warfarin blood levels and anticoagulant effect to increase. Patients may need a warfarin dose reduction and more frequent INR checks.

interactions.title: Elevated Statin Levels: Diltiazem + Simvastatin
interactions.detail: Diltiazem (calcium channel blocker) inhibits CYP3A4, raising simvastatin blood levels and increasing myopathy risk. The FDA recommends limiting simvastatin to 10mg/day when combined with diltiazem.

interactions.title: Severe Hearing/Kidney Damage: Furosemide + Gentamicin
interactions.detail: Both furosemide (a loop diuretic) and gentamicin (an aminoglycoside antibiotic) are individually toxic to the inner ear (ototoxic) and kidneys (nephrotoxic). Combined, the risk of permanent hearing loss and kidney failure is greatly amplified.

interactions.title: Fatal Respiratory Depression: Diazepam + Oxycodone
interactions.detail: Both diazepam (a benzodiazepine) and oxycodone (an opioid) suppress the central nervous system and slow breathing. Together, they dramatically increase the risk of respiratory depression, unconsciousness, and fatal overdose.

interactions.title: CNS/Respiratory Depression: Tramadol + Diazepam
interactions.detail: Combining tramadol (opioid-like analgesic) with diazepam (benzodiazepine sedative) creates additive central nervous system depression. This combination significantly increases the risk of sedation, slowed breathing, and overdose death.

interactions.title: Severe Blood Pressure Drop: Sildenafil + Nitrates
interactions.detail: Both sildenafil (for erectile dysfunction or pulmonary hypertension) and nitrates like isosorbide mononitrate cause blood vessel dilation. Together, they cause a catastrophic drop in blood pressure that can lead to fainting, heart attack, and death. This combination is absolutely contraindicated.

interactions.title: Respiratory Depression: Codeine + Diazepam
interactions.detail: Codeine (an opioid pain reliever) and diazepam (a benzodiazepine) both depress the central nervous system. Their combined effect on breathing is greater than the sum of their individual effects, creating serious risk of respiratory arrest.
